your decks. You will be able to build and play with
this deck by collecting the cards in this list.

can obtain only one of the nine ex Starter Decks.

CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0010:
The number 16 brings to mind
Dragonite! It can fly in spite of its big
and bulky physique. It circles the globe
in just 16 hours.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0020:
You’ve collected 25 cards. 25 is
Pikachu’s National Pokédex
number! When several Pikachu
gather, their electricity can build
and cause lightning storms.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0030:
You’ve collected 50 cards. 50 is
Diglett’s National Pokédex number!
It lives about one yard underground,
where it feeds on plant roots. It
sometimes appears aboveground.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0040:
The number 80 brings to mind
Tentacruel! Its 80 tentacles can
stretch and shrink freely. Tentacruel
ensnares prey in a net of spread-out
tentacles, delivering venomous stings
to its catch.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0050:
The number 100 brings to mind
Machop! Its whole body is composed
of muscles. Even though it’s the size
of a human child, it can hurl 100
grown-ups.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0060:
The number 151 brings to mind the
Pokédex! A total of 151 Pokémon
were introduced in [Ctrl:Italic ]Pokémon Red[/Ctrl:Italic]
and [Ctrl:Italic ]Pokémon Blue[/Ctrl:Italic].
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0070:
The number 180 brings to mind
Noctowl! When it needs to think, it
rotates its head 180 degrees to
sharpen its intellectual power.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0080:
You’ve collected 250 cards. 250 is
Ho-Oh’s National Pokédex
number! It will reveal itself before
a pure-hearted Trainer by shining
its bright, rainbow-colored wings.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0090:
The number 300 brings to mind
Florges! It is said that there was once
a Florges that protected the garden of
a castle for over 300 years.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0100:
The number 500 brings to mind
Spiritomb! It was bound to a fissure in
an odd keystone as punishment for
misdeeds 500 years ago.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0110:
You’ve collected 777 cards. 777 is
Togedemaru’s National Pokédex
number! When it’s in trouble, it
curls up into a ball, makes its fur
spikes stand on end, and then
discharges electricity indiscriminately.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0120:
The number 1,000 brings to mind
Jirachi! It is said to have the ability to
grant any wish for just one week
every thousand years.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0130:
The number 1,500 brings to mind
Gimmighoul! This Pokémon was born
inside a treasure chest about 1,500
years ago. It sucks the life-force out of
scoundrels who try to steal the
treasure.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0140:
The number 2,000 brings to mind
Conkeldurr! It is thought that
Conkeldurr taught humans how to
make concrete more than 2,000
years ago.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0150:
The number 5,000 brings to mind
Alakazam! It is said to have an IQ of
approximately 5,000. Its overflowing
psychokinetic powers cause headaches
to anyone nearby.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0160:
The number 10,000 brings to mind
Wartortle! It is said to live 10,000
years. Its furry tail is popular as a
symbol of longevity.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0170:
The number 15,000 brings to mind
Toxtricity! The jolts of electricity it
launches by violently strumming the
protrusions on its chest easily exceed
15,000 volts.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0180:
The number 20,000 brings to mind
Claydol! This mysterious Pokémon
started life as an ancient clay figurine
made over 20,000 years ago.
CardTotalMilestone_TIPS_0190:
The number 100,000 brings to mind
Raichu! It can loose 100,000-volt
bursts of electricity, instantly downing
foes several times its size.

This Pokémon rides on its tail while it uses
its psychic powers to levitate. It attacks with
star-shaped thunderbolts.
FLAVOR_956:
Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said
that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together,
lightning will fall immediately after.
FLAVOR_957:
This Pokémon absorbs electricity from telephone
poles. It shorts out the electricity stored inside its
body to create noises.
FLAVOR_958:
Its dislike of water makes it take shelter under
the eaves of houses in rain. It uses pom-poms
made of sparks for cheering.
FLAVOR_959:
This selfish, attention-seeking Pokémon stores
poison and electricity in two different sacs inside
its body.
FLAVOR_96:
When this ill-tempered Pokémon runs wild, it
shoots lightning from its mane in all directions.
FLAVOR_960:
It floats using the electricity stored in its body.
When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will
float higher off the ground.
FLAVOR_961:
What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs
for discharging the electricity generated by
Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo.
FLAVOR_962:
This Pokémon will look into your eyes and read
the contents of your heart. If it finds evil there,
it promptly hides away.
FLAVOR_963:
Brave and prideful, this Pokémon dashes airily
through the forest, its steps aided by the psychic
power stored in the fur on its fetlocks.
FLAVOR_964:
To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly
in the darkness. It is never first to attack.
FLAVOR_965:
Its growls make its opponents uneasy. This
laid-back Pokémon tends to sleep half the day.
FLAVOR_966:
It can make most any Pokémon run away
by opening its big mouth to reveal its
thick fangs.
FLAVOR_967:
It is highly attuned to the emotions of people
and Pokémon. It hides if it senses hostility.
FLAVOR_968:
The cheerful spirit of its Trainer gives it energy
for its psychokinetic power. It spins and dances
when happy.
FLAVOR_969:
It unleashes psychokinetic energy at full power
when protecting a Trainer it has bonded closely
with.
FLAVOR_97:
While one alone doesn’t have much power,
a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful
as lightning.
FLAVOR_970:
While shining a light and pretending to be a
guide, it leeches off the life-force of any who
follow it.
FLAVOR_971:
The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs
around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.
FLAVOR_972:
It absorbs spirits, which it then burns. By waving
the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a
hypnotic trance.
FLAVOR_973:
Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization
method that can control the feelings of those who
hear it.
FLAVOR_974:
The light that streams out from the holes in the
pumpkin can hypnotize and control the people
and Pokémon that see it.
FLAVOR_975:
In the darkness of a new-moon night, Gourgeist
will come knocking. Whoever answers the door
will be swept off to the afterlife.
FLAVOR_976:
Sinistea gets into your body when you drink it,
and then it steals your vitality from within. It also
tastes awful.
FLAVOR_977:
These Pokémon multiply by creeping into teapots
and pouring themselves into leftover tea.
FLAVOR_978:
This Pokémon never leaves its Trainer’s side.
It predicts their actions with its psychic power
and takes care of their day-to-day needs.
FLAVOR_979:
No matter how high a place it falls from, this
Pokémon can save itself by rolling into a ball
and bouncing.
FLAVOR_98:
They coil around foes and shock them with
electricity-generating organs that seem simply
to be circular patterns.
FLAVOR_980:
The spikes on its body are made up of its
hardened hide. It rolls up and attacks foes
with its spikes.
FLAVOR_981:
Always brimming with power, it passes time by
lifting boulders. Doing so makes it even stronger.
FLAVOR_982:
Its formidable body never gets tired. It helps
people by doing work such as the moving of
heavy goods.
FLAVOR_983:
With four arms that react more quickly than it
can think, it can execute many punches at once.
FLAVOR_984:
This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased
mother. Sometimes Cubone’s dreams make it cry,
but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.
FLAVOR_985:
It meditates to heighten its inner energy and to
float in the air. It eats one berry a day.
FLAVOR_986:
It elegantly avoids attacks with dance-like
steps, then launches a devastating blow in
the same motion.
FLAVOR_987:
When it detects a noise, it starts to move.
The energy core inside it makes this Pokémon
slightly warm to the touch.
FLAVOR_988:
It relies on sound in order to monitor what’s in its
vicinity. When angered, it will attack without ever
changing the direction it’s facing.
FLAVOR_989:
It makes its way swiftly through the soil by putting
both claws together and rotating at high speed.
FLAVOR_99:
They crawl out of the ocean using their arms.
They will attack prey on shore and immediately
drag it into the ocean.
FLAVOR_990:
This Pokémon is selfish and likes to be pampered.
It can also inflict grievous wounds on its Trainer
just by playing around.
FLAVOR_991:
A single bite of Tyrantrum’s massive jaws will
demolish a car. This Pokémon was the king of the
ancient world.
FLAVOR_992:
The boss chooses 10 members of the group to
go out hunting. The hunting party will evenly split
the food they find with the rest of the group.
FLAVOR_993:
The leader, known as the brass, uses its
extendible horn to issue orders to the others
when it’s time to change formation.
FLAVOR_994:
In this form, it draws on the power of stone.
Its body is rock-solid, protecting it from all
manner of attacks.
FLAVOR_995:
Deeply proud and keenly smart, this Pokémon
moves with cunning during battle and relentlessly
attacks enemies’ weak points.
FLAVOR_996:
This Pokémon is one tough opponent. Not only
does it have formidable physical abilities, but it’s
also not above fighting dirty.
FLAVOR_997:
Alolan Grimer will gladly gobble up any kind
of trash, making it a widely used and popular
Pokémon at garbage disposal facilities.
FLAVOR_998:
What look like fangs and claws are actually
crystallized poison that will afflict you at a
mere touch, so don’t get too close.
FLAVOR_999:
Thought to be the oldest form of Zigzagoon,
it moves in zigzags and wreaks havoc upon
its surroundings.

Take a look at the Greninja in the 
Active Spot.

Abilities are special powers that Pokémon
have that are different from attacks.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00300:
Unlike attacks, using an Ability does not
end your turn.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00400: There are Abilities that work all the time.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00500:
This Greninja has the 
Water Shuriken Ability.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00600:
This powerful Ability lets you do damage 
in addition to its attack damage.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00800:
You’ve attached an Energy, so use the
attack to Knock Out Jynx.
battle_tutorial_attack_message_00100:
Knock Out your opponent’s Pokémon to
earn points.
battle_tutorial_attack_message_00200:
If you’re the first to reach 3 points,
you win the battle.
battle_tutorial_attack_message_00400:
Use Pikachu’s Gnaw attack to Knock Out
your opponent’s Eevee.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00100:
Start your turn by drawing a card from
your deck.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00200:
You can play cards that are in your hand
during your turn.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00300:
Play Pikachu from your hand to
your Bench.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00400:
If you have no Pokémon left in play, you
lose the battle.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00500:
But now, even if your Active Pokémon is
Knocked Out, you don’t need to worry!
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00600:
Eevee in the Active Spot was
Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00700:
Choose a Benched Pokémon to move to
the Active Spot.

When it is your turn, an Energy is
generated in the Energy Zone.

You can also see the Energy that will be
generated during your next turn.
Pikachu now has one Lightning Energy.
It can now use its attack, Gnaw.

Energy can be attached to a
Benched Pokémon, too.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_002:
By attaching Energy to a Benched Pokémon
you will be prepared to attack.

Pikachu already has one Lightning Energy,
so it can use its attack.

use its attack.

here with the correct Evolution Pokémon.

Active Spot.

Evolve Pokémon in play by putting Evolution
Pokémon from your hand on top of them.

attacks after evolving.

attached Energy and any damage.

this turn.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00100:
There are other types of cards that are
useful in battle besides Pokémon cards.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00200: Take a look at the cards in your hand.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00400:
Trainer cards are divided into Items and
Supporters depending on usage and effect.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00500: This is the Item card, Potion.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00600:
Playing this card will heal one of your
Pokémon’s HP.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00800: Play Potion to heal Pikachu’s HP.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00900:
You may play as many Item cards as you
like during your turn.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_01000:
Since Pikachu’s HP was healed, it
didn’t get Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_001:
Cards aren’t only for collecting. They can
also be used in battle.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_002: Take a look at the Pikachu card.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_003:
Pokémon have HP. When they lose all of
their HP, they are Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_004:
Here you can find a card’s attacks. With
these, you can attack your opponent’s
Pokémon and use the attacks’ effects.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_005:
You and your opponent’s Pokémon battle
one another as you try to Knock Out all
of their Pokémon one by one.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_006:
In a battle, you can use cards you’ve
collected to face off against your opponent.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_007:
In this guide, you can battle with cards
that have been set up for you.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_008:
The cards near you are your in-play zone,
and the cards on the other side are your
opponent’s in-play zone.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_009:
This is your Active Spot, and it’s where
your Pokémon battle using attacks.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_010:
Pokémon in the Active Spot are referred
to as Active Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_011:
This is your Bench, and it’s where you put
Pokémon that can switch with your Active
Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_012:
Pokémon on the Bench are referred to as
Benched Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_014:
Your cards are placed here face down, and
you draw one on your turn.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_016:
You can have up to 10 cards in your hand,
and you use these cards during the battle.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_017:
Starting in the next part of the guide, we’ll
go through the steps of a battle.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_001: You have one Trainer card in your hand.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_002: Let’s take a good look at it.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_003:
This is the Pokémon Tool card,
Giant Cape.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_004:
You can attach Pokémon Tools to your Active
Pokémon or to your Benched Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_005:
Once a Pokémon Tool has been attached to
a Pokémon, it remains attached until the
Pokémon leaves play.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_006:
You can use as many Pokémon Tools during
your turn as you’d like, but each Pokémon can
have only one attached at a time.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_007:
This card gives +20 HP to the Pokémon it’s
attached to.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_008:
If your Pokémon is attacked on your
opponent’s next turn, it will be Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_010:
Your Pokémon’s remaining HP is now 70, and
it looks like it’ll be able to withstand
one attack.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_011: Let’s attach an Energy and end your turn.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_012:
Because its HP was increased, Raichu wasn’t
Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0040:
Before starting the battle, let’s set up
your Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0050:
First, put a Pokémon from your hand into
the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0060: Take a good look at the cards in your hand.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0070: You can play any Pokémon that says Basic.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0080: Place a Basic Pokémon in the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0090:
Once you’re done setting up your Active
Pokémon, next is setting up your Bench.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0100:
During a real battle, you have the option to
set up your Bench.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0110: For this guide, let’s practice setting it up.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0120:
You can put a Basic Pokémon here,
just like in the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0130:
Once you’ve set up your Pokémon,
go ahead and tap Start Battle.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0140: Now, you’re ready to begin the battle.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00100:
You can switch your Active Pokémon with
your Benched Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00300: Take a look at Pikachu’s Retreat Cost.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00500: The Retreat Cost is one Energy.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00600:
Let’s retreat Pikachu and switch it 
with Raichu.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00700:
If you retreat, the Energy cost will be
discarded from that Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00800: You can retreat once per turn.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00900:
You can still use an attack even if you
retreated during that turn.
battle_tutorial_special_condition_messag: Take a look at Grimer in the Active Spot.

It says that your opponent’s Active
Pokémon is now Poisoned.

Attacks can have all kinds of effects like this
apart from just damage.

This attack can make your opponent’s
Pokémon Poisoned.

Use Poison Gas to make your opponent’s
Pokémon Poisoned.

You made your opponent’s Caterpie
Poisoned.

Poisoned Pokémon take 10 damage during
Pokémon Checkup.

Pokémon will recover from Special
Conditions, such as Poisoned, when they
move to the Bench.

Apart from Poisoned, there are other
Special Conditions such as Paralyzed and
Asleep.
For more information, check out Tips.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00100: You have one Trainer card in your hand.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00200: Let’s take a good look at it.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00300: This is called a Stadium card.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00400:
When a Stadium card is in play, it has an effect
on both you and your opponent.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00500:
You can play only 1 Stadium card from your
hand during your turn, and it stays in play.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00600: Only 1 Stadium card can be in play at a time.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00700:
When a Stadium with a different name is put
in play, discard the Stadium that was
previously in play and replace it.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00800:
You can’t play a Stadium card with the 
same name as the Stadium already in play.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00900:
This card makes attacks used by both
players’ Stage 1 Pokémon do +10 damage
to their opponent’s Active Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01000: Let’s take a look at this Charmeleon card.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01100:
Because Charmeleon is a Stage 1 Pokémon,
we can apply the effect of Training Area and
increase the damage done by its attacks.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01300:
We discarded the Stadium that your opponent
put in play and replaced it with Training Area.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01400:
Now, Charmeleon’s attack can Knock Out
Wartortle.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00100:
You only have one Trainer card in
your hand.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00200: Let’s take a good look at it.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00300:
This is the Supporter card,
Professor’s Research.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00400:
Unlike Item cards, you can only use one
Supporter card on your turn.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00500:
If you play Professor’s Research, you can
draw two cards from your deck.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00600: At this rate, Pikachu will get Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00700:
Play Professor’s Research and draw cards
from your deck.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00800: It looks like you drew a Raichu.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00900:
Let’s evolve Pikachu into Raichu and use
an attack.
battle_tutorial_top_training_btn_07:
Attach Energy to your
Benched Pokémon!
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00200: Let’s take a closer look at the Snorlax card.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00450:
These are called Colorless Energy. The
symbols mean any type of Energy can be
used.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00500:
When you can’t use an attack, tap the
End Turn button to end your turn.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00600:
Energy will generate in your Energy Zone
during your turn.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00700:
Attach a fourth Energy to Snorlax and use
its attack.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00400:
Let’s take a closer look at the opponent’s
Squirtle card.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00500:
Most Pokémon have a type that they’re
weak to.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00700:
Let’s use an attack by your
Lightning-type Pikachu.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00900:
You can do a lot of damage by attacking
Weaknesses.

first_tutorial_dialog_01_page_01:
Welcome to
Pokémon Trading Card Game Pocket!
first_tutorial_dialog_01_page_02:
In this game, you can enjoy building a Pokémon
Trading Card Game collection on your mobile
device.

To begin, please tell us your player name.
first_tutorial_dialog_02_page_01:
This is the end of the basic tutorial.

Now try exploring some of the game’s features!
first_tutorial_dialog_02_page_02:
Pack stamina refills, so you can open booster
packs every day.
first_tutorial_dialog_02_page_03:
Try unlocking new features by completing
beginner missions, getting player EXP, and
increasing your level.
first_tutorial_dialog_08_page_01:
In Wonder Pick, you can get one of the cards
(chosen randomly) from a booster pack that was
opened by another player.

Note: That player will not lose any cards.
first_tutorial_dialog_08_page_02:
Wonder picks are updated at regular intervals.
Booster packs opened by your friends may also
appear as wonder picks.

Try to check in regularly to see what’s new.
first_tutorial_dialog_08_page_03:
Wonder picking requires wonder stamina, which
recovers over time.

You can reduce the time it takes until wonder
stamina recovers by using items.
first_tutorial_dialog_08_page_04:
There are also special kinds of wonder picks that
may appear, like bonus picks and Chansey picks.
first_tutorial_dialog_08_page_05:
An expired wonder pick can be made available
again by using a rewind watch.
first_tutorial_message_01_page_01:
Let’s take a look at the cards you’ve registered
in the card dex.
first_tutorial_message_02_page_01:
Tap on the mission you completed to
claim a reward.
first_tutorial_message_03_page_01:
You can open a booster pack once your
pack stamina is full.
first_tutorial_message_03_page_02:
It looks like you’ll be able to open a pack if
you wait just a little longer.
first_tutorial_message_04_page_01:
Your pack stamina has recovered.
Try opening a booster pack.
first_tutorial_message_05_page_01:
Notifications can let you know when you’re able
to open packs.

You can turn notifications on by going to the
menu, Other, and then Settings.
first_tutorial_message_06_page_01:
Your pack stamina has fully recovered.
Please try opening a booster pack.
first_tutorial_message_06_page_03:
Please enjoy playing
Pokémon Trading Card Game Pocket!
first_tutorial_message_07_page_01:
You got player EXP from opening packs, so
you’ve leveled up!
first_tutorial_message_07_page_02:
You’ve just unlocked the Wonder Pick
feature. Let’s take a look at it.
first_tutorial_message_08_page_01:
Results from booster packs opened by
other players are shown here.
first_tutorial_message_09_page_01: Let’s try wonder picking for real!
first_tutorial_pack_open_body: Please choose the booster pack you want.
first_tutorial_player_setting_body: Please select your player icon and player name.
first_tutorial_player_setting_caution: Note: Your player icon can be changed anytime.
first_tutorial_return_to_title_body:
Returning to the title screen to download
necessary game data.
first_tutorial_user_name_donfirm_caution:
Your player name cannot be changed again for
30 days.
function_tutorial_dialog_01_page_01:
Pack stamina refills, so you can use it to open
booster packs every day.

Pack stamina recovery time can be reduced by
using pack hourglasses or Poké gold.
function_tutorial_dialog_01_page_02:
You can tap on the button on the bottom-right
part of the screen if you want to open a different
booster pack.

You can then choose a booster pack from among
those that have become available so far.
function_tutorial_dialog_01_page_03:
You will be notified when your pack stamina has
recovered and you can open a pack.

And remember, you can open your choice of
booster packs every day.
function_tutorial_dialog_02_page_01:
You can tap a card to enlarge it and view its
information in detail.
function_tutorial_dialog_02_page_02:
You can also see cards you do not own if you tap
the card dex toggle switch.
function_tutorial_dialog_02_page_03:
If you obtain duplicates of a card, you can obtain
flair which can be used to change that card’s
appearance.

Please see the videos for further details.
function_tutorial_dialog_03_page_02:
You can tap this icon if you want to see this
explanation again.

If you’re unsure of anything else, you can try
checking Tips.
function_tutorial_dialog_04_page_01:
In Binders, you can create binders with cards you
have collected.

There are a variety of covers that can be obtained
in a number of ways, like from the Shop or by
completing missions.
function_tutorial_dialog_04_page_02:
You can share the binders you’ve created with
friends and other players.

You can view what other players have shared in
Social Hub.
function_tutorial_dialog_05_page_01: Try creating binders that are uniquely yours!
function_tutorial_dialog_05_page_02:
You can tap this icon if you want to see this
explanation again.

If you’re unsure of anything else, you can try
checking Tips.
function_tutorial_dialog_06_page_01:
In Display Boards, you can place cards on
backdrops and show them off.

There are a variety of backdrops that can be
obtained in a number of ways, like from the Shop
or by completing missions.
function_tutorial_dialog_06_page_02:
You can share the display boards you’ve created
with friends or other players.

You can view what other players have shared in
Social Hub.
function_tutorial_dialog_07_page_01:
Try creating display boards that are
uniquely yours!
function_tutorial_dialog_07_page_02:
You can tap this icon if you want to see this
explanation again.

If you’re unsure of anything else, you can try
checking Tips.
function_tutorial_dialog_08_page_01:
You will receive a deck once you complete part 06
of the battle guide, “Evolve your Pokémon!”

Play your way through the battle guide
to receive other rewards, like pack hourglasses.
function_tutorial_dialog_09_page_01: In My Decks, you can build decks to use in battle.
function_tutorial_dialog_09_page_02: A deck is made up of a set of 20 cards.
function_tutorial_dialog_09_page_03:
You can also build a deck using Auto-build.

All you have to do is select Auto-build, then one
or more types, and a deck will be automatically
built using cards you own.
function_tutorial_dialog_09_page_04:
You can also change your playmat, card sleeves,
and Pokémon coin.

These can be obtained in a number of ways, like
from the Shop or by completing missions.
function_tutorial_dialog_09_page_05:
You can tap this icon if you want to see this
explanation again.

If you’re unsure of anything else, you can try
checking Tips.
function_tutorial_dialog_11_page_01:
Rental decks are a kind of deck that let you
borrow a set of 20 cards to use in battle.
function_tutorial_dialog_11_page_02:
Rental decks are obtained mainly by completing
deck missions.

You can see the rental decks you have obtained
from the Deck Menu.
function_tutorial_dialog_11_page_03: A rental deck has a limited number of uses.
function_tutorial_dialog_12_page_01: You can use theme deck lists to easily build decks.
function_tutorial_dialog_12_page_02:
If you select a theme deck list when building a
deck, a deck will be built using cards you own.

To build a theme deck, you must own all the cards
required by the theme deck list.
function_tutorial_dialog_14_page_01:
There are all sorts of missions available.

You can try to complete as many as you can to
earn rewards.
function_tutorial_dialog_14_page_02:
For missions that involve collecting specific cards,
you will be able to see additional details about the
ones you need to collect.

You can try to collect them by opening packs and
wonder picking.
function_tutorial_dialog_14_page_03:
You accumulate pack points by opening booster
packs. Pack points can be used to get cards of
your choosing.
function_tutorial_dialog_16_page_01:
You accumulate pack points by using pack stamina
to open booster packs.

You can exchange a set amount of pack points for
cards of your choosing.
function_tutorial_dialog_16_page_02:
Opening booster packs of a given expansion earns
you pack points for that expansion.

Those points can be exchanged only for cards that
appear in that expansion.
function_tutorial_dialog_16_page_03:
An expansion is a group of similarly labeled
booster packs.

You can view different expansions by tapping
Select other booster packs at the bottom-right
part of the packs screen.
function_tutorial_dialog_17_page_02:
As you collect certain cards, you will be able to
obtain rental decks which let you try a deck in
battle.

There is a limit to how many times you can use a
particular rental deck.
function_tutorial_dialog_17_page_03:
Once you collect the 20 cards listed in a deck
mission for a given deck, you will obtain its theme
deck list.

You can then build that same deck anytime by
tapping Build New from the Decks screen.
function_tutorial_dialog_18_page_01:
If you run out of pack stamina, you can’t open any
packs until your stamina has recovered.

Let’s try reducing recovery time with pack
hourglasses.
function_tutorial_dialog_19_page_01:
You can get pack hourglasses in a variety of ways,
like when increasing your player level or as
mission rewards, and you can use them as soon as
you get them!
function_tutorial_dialog_19_page_02:
When you subscribe to the premium pass, you can
open one more pack every day.

First-time subscribers to the premium pass may
use it at no cost for two weeks. You can subscribe
from the Shop.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_01:
First, choose one friend to trade with and send a
trade offer.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_02:
Then, choose just one card to send to that friend,
and offer it to trade. After you send your trade
offer, wait for their response.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_03:
When you get a response, a notification will
appear on the Trade screen. View the card
they’re offering and tap OK.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_04:
Once a trade agreement is reached, you and your
trade partner’s cards will be exchanged.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_05:
In order to trade, you need trade stamina.
Trade stamina recovers over time. You can
use items to reduce the time it takes to recover.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_06:
Trades can be done with cards of the same rarity.
To trade high-rarity cards, you need shinedust.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_07:
Shinedust can be obtained when you acquire
cards already registered in your card dex, as 
mission rewards, and so forth.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_08:
You can now share which cards are on your
wishlist when trading with other players.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_09:
You can wishlist cards from the card details screen
in My Cards.
function_tutorial_dialog_20_page_10:
Up to three wishlisted cards can be set to display
on your profile and on your friends list when
trading.
You can set these cards on the profile screen.
function_tutorial_dialog_21_page_01:
You can check the card that your trade partner is
planning to send you. If you want the card, you can
proceed to the next step. You can also decline the
offer.
function_tutorial_dialog_21_page_02:
To receive that card from your trade partner, you
choose just one card to send to them in response.
Once you’ve responded, wait for your trade
partner’s OK.
function_tutorial_dialog_21_page_03:
When your trade partner accepts the trade, a
notification will appear on the Trade screen. Once
you get the notification you can receive their card.
function_tutorial_dialog_24_page_01:
In Ranked Matches, there is a rank system that
goes from Beginner Rank to Master Ball Rank.
You can go up in rank based on the points you
get when you win battles.
function_tutorial_dialog_24_page_02:
In Master Ball Rank, the top players will have their
ranking displayed.
function_tutorial_dialog_24_page_03:
The ranked match season will change about once
a month. After a season ends, players can get
emblems based on their rank at the time the
season ended.
function_tutorial_dialog_25_page_01:
Choose a card you will send to the other person.

You will receive from them a card of the same
rarity as the card you chose.
function_tutorial_dialog_26_page_01:
You can apply flair to cards. 
If you offer a card with flair, you’ll receive a card
with flair in return.
Note: Once the trade agreement has been
reached, the flair on your card will disappear.
function_tutorial_dialog_27_page_01:
Choose a card to send to the other person.

Only cards of the same rarity can be traded.
function_tutorial_dialog_28_page_01:
Cards that have flair can only be traded with other
cards that have flair.
You can attach any flair that you own from the
Edit Card screen.
Note: Once the trade agreement has been
reached, the flair on your card will disappear.
function_tutorial_dialog_34_page_01:
Select an item or flair to see which cards you can
exchange for it.
function_tutorial_dialog_34_page_02: You can exchange multiple cards at once.
function_tutorial_dialog_35_page_01:
Choose a friend to send a card to. You can send
a card to the same friend once per day.
function_tutorial_dialog_35_page_02:
Next, choose just one card to give to
that friend and send it to them.
function_tutorial_dialog_35_page_03: The card will be sent to your friend’s Gifts.
function_tutorial_dialog_36_page_01:
A favoriting feature has been added to the friends
list. Favorited friends are shown at the top of the
friends list, so they will be easier to find when
trading, for example.
function_tutorial_dialog_36_page_02:
To favorite a friend, tap Favorites at the top-right
of the friends list.

pack_offer_ratio_caution_01:
When a pack is opened, the steps listed below will be carried out in sequence. (Further details follow.)

Step 1: Pack Selection
Step 2: Card Selection

About step 1: Pack Selection
Pack selection is the first selection process that is carried out.
In pack selection, a pack to be opened will be selected so that step 2, card selection, can occur.
Please see the Offering Rates tab to confirm the category names, offering rates, and number of cards in the packs that are generated.

About step 2: Card Selection
After the pack to be opened is decided in step 1, pack selection, step 2, card selection, is carried out.
In card selection, the cards that are actually generated will be selected.
The categories of cards offered and the offering rates differ for each pack. The number of cards in the packs may also differ. For example, if a “regular” pack is selected, cards will be generated as displayed in the categories, offering rates, and number of cards for “regular packs.” If a “rare” pack is selected, cards will be generated as displayed in the categories, offering rates, and number of cards for “rare packs.”

• Cards from packs not selected in pack selection will not be generated. For example, if a “regular” pack is selected, cards will be generated from “regular” packs. (Cards from “rare” packs will not be generated.)
• Please see the Offering Rates tab to confirm the specific probability rates for card selection.
• The offering rate displayed for each card is the offering rate after the pack category is decided in pack selection.
• The cards in a pack are selected one at a time.
• Booster packs that are available for a limited time only may be offered again after the availability period has ended.
• Cards available in this pack may also be available in packs added at a future date.
• The availability period and details are subject to change without warning.

Additional notes:
• It’s possible for the offering rate of cards included in the same pack to be different.
• It’s possible for the order of the cards in the results to differ from the order that the cards were actually selected in.
• It’s possible for the same card to be selected and offered two or more times in the same pack as duplicates.
• The offering rates are cut off after the third decimal place and may not equal 100% when added together.
• Actual offering rates have not been rounded up or down.
• Changes may be made, such as adjustments to card details or bans on certain cards from being used, as a result of error fixes or adjustments made to maintain a fair battle environment.
• The language of the cards will be the app’s selected language at the time a pack is opened.
• The language of cards already obtained will stay the same as it was at the time they were obtained and will not be affected if the app’s selected language is changed after they were obtained.

About “[Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher guaranteed” packs
• If the condition below is fulfilled, the next time a pack from the same expansion as the pack for which the condition has been fulfilled is opened, a [Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher card will be generated.

Condition: A [Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher card did not get generated after 12 consecutive openings of packs from the same expansion.
Note: Information related to fulfilling the condition, such as the current number of consecutive openings, or the number of openings remaining to fulfill the condition, will not be displayed.

• If the condition is fulfilled, the pack categories selected during step 1, pack selection, will change.
• During pack selection, the “[Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher guaranteed” pack category will be added but will not be the only category offered. It is possible for “rare” or “regular +1 card” pack categories to be offered instead.
Note: In that case, a [Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher card is still guaranteed to be generated.
• For more details, please see the “Offering Rates” tab.
pack_offer_ratio_caution_02:
• A “regular” pack will not be selected if the conditions for the booster pack in this category to be generated have been fulfilled.
• In place of it, the booster pack in this category will be selected.
• The selection probability will be the same as the offering rates of a “regular” pack.
• Please check the Attention section for information on pack generation conditions.
pack_offer_ratio_caution_03:
• A “regular” or “regular + 1 card” pack will not be selected if the conditions for the booster pack in this category to be generated have been fulfilled.
• In place of it, the booster pack in this category will be selected.
• The selection probability will be that of a “regular” and a “regular + 1 card” pack combined.
• Please check the Attention section for information on pack generation conditions.

subscription_contract_attention_01:
[Ctrl:Bold ]■ About the contract
• When you subscribe to the premium pass, your subscription will be automatically renewed every month unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the premium pass expiration date.[/Ctrl:Bold]
• For more information on premium pass cancellation methods, reimbursement options, payment periods and methods, transferring data, and changing devices, please refer to Customer Support.
• If you cancel your subscription, the monthly cost will not be prorated.
• If you choose to cancel your plan before it has reached its renewal date, you will still have premium pass benefits until the expiration date.
• Digital content such as in-game currencies and in-game items are offered as in-game licensed materials.

■ About the no-cost trial
• The first time you purchase a premium pass, you won’t be charged for the first 14 days.
• After completing the no-cost trial, your plan will automatically be converted to a paid premium pass plan that renews automatically.
• If you would like to only subscribe to the premium pass while it is available at no cost, please cancel your subscription at least 24 hours before the end of the no-cost trial. For information on cancellation methods, please refer to Customer Support.
• If you repeatedly make inappropriate use of the no-cost trial with methods other than those intended by our company, we may suspend your account or take other actions.
<color=#F23E44>• In some cases, the one-time two-week no-cost trial may not be applied due to app store specifications.
• Please confirm that the no-cost trial is displayed on the app store payment screen before subscribing.</color>
• If the App[C:Nbsp ]Store or Google[C:Nbsp ]Play deems that a no-cost trial is not applicable, even if it is your first subscription, the no-cost trial may not be applied.
• Please check the App[C:Nbsp ]Store or Google[C:Nbsp ]Play purchase screen to confirm whether or not the no-cost trial is applicable. If the no-cost trial is not displayed on the purchase screen, please note that the no-cost trial will not be applied and a fee will be charged at the time of subscription.

■ About benefits
Benefit 1: You can open one more pack every day
• A new pack stamina gauge will be added. That gauge will let you open one additional pack every 24 hours.
• The maximum storage that pack stamina added by the premium pass can reach is two packs worth.
• Premium pass pack stamina cannot be recovered using items such as pack hourglasses.

Benefit 2: You can take on premium missions that let you get promo cards
• You’ll be able to take on premium missions, and if you complete those missions, you can get premium tickets and other rewards.
• If you collect premium tickets, you can exchange set amounts of them for various items.
• Premium missions and the items that can be exchanged for using premium tickets are regularly refreshed/changed. After a refresh, the items cannot be claimed.
• You can refer to the following screens for information about items or their availability periods:
The Premium tab on the Missions screen
The Premium tab on the Shop screen
• Cards received will be cards of the app’s selected language.
• If you cancel a subscription and then subscribe again, you will not be able to obtain items you already claimed.
subscription_contract_attention_02_01:
■To iOS users:
• If your AppIe Account has already been used for a trial, you will no longer be eligible for a 14-day no-cost trial period.
• To confirm the expiration date of your pass, open the Settings app on your device, tap on your Apple Account, then tap Subscriptions.
Note: These options may appear differently on your device, depending on your OS version.
subscription_contract_attention_02_02:
■ To Android users:
• If your Google Account has already been used for a trial, you will no longer be eligible for a 14-day no-cost trial period.
• To confirm the expiration date of your pass, open the Play Store, tap on your profile icon, then select Payments & Subscriptions. You should find the information under Subscriptions.

longer be able to play using it. Even if you link

continue playing with the save data, and you will
not be able to restore it.
